clue.text: Clumsily inflate a jet for a pirate

indicators.note: done clumsily, the letters of these words are bungled into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone fumbles with an inflatable jet while dressing up as a buccaneer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clumsily' rearranges INFLATE A JET into the name; 'for' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean Lafitte was a real early nineteenth-century privateer and smuggler in the Gulf of Mexico.

clue.text: Lamb is the final incomplete liar

indicators.note: the final letter of the word just before it is wanted
an incomplete word has lost its tail, so the closing letter goes; that the four letters also run across 'incomplete liar' is a coincidence

explanation.surface: Someone named Lamb is branded the ultimate half-hearted fibber.
explanation.walkthrough: 'final' takes E from 'the'; 'incomplete' drops the R from 'liar', leaving LIA.
explanation.definitionFit: The essayist Charles Lamb wrote under the pen name used in his Essays of Elia.

clue.text: Greenest bird's home lined with a little ivy

indicators.note: a home lined with something has that material set just inside its walls

parts.note: a bird's home is its nest

indicators.note: a little of the word, with its last letter cut off

explanation.surface: A fresh-looking bird's nest has been lined with a sprig of ivy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' trims the last letter from 'ivy'; 'lined with' sets that, after A, just inside the home.
explanation.definitionFit: Green means inexperienced or unworldly, so the greenest person is the most innocent and unsophisticated.

clue.text: Transport of tautological interpretation

indicators.note: the answer is formed out of part of the following word

explanation.surface: A vehicle is described in pointlessly repetitive terms.
explanation.walkthrough: The four letters sit inside 'tautological'; 'interpretation' just completes the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Auto is a short word for a motor car, a means of transport.

clue.text: Bursts out of the broken stirrup

indicators.note: a broken word has its letters smashed and reassembled

explanation.surface: A rider's foot breaks free from a snapped stirrup.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broken' rearranges STIRRUP; 'out of the' is link material, though 'Bursts out' tempts as one phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To irrupt is to break or rush in violently, so irrupts means bursts in.

clue.text: About to race around with allowance for waste

indicators.note: the race letters are placed around the other piece

parts.note: TT is the Tourist Trophy motorcycle race on the Isle of Man
re is Latin-derived for about or concerning

explanation.surface: A runner about to race round a track gets some leeway for wasted effort.
explanation.walkthrough: The TT is the Isle of Man motorcycle race series, and 'around' puts it either side of the Latin-derived 'about'. 'to' and 'with' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Tret was an old trading allowance deducted for goods spoiled or lost in transit.

clue.text: It takes a sucker to shift dirt like this

definitions.text: It takes a sucker to shift dirt like this

parts.words: It takes a sucker to shift dirt like this
parts.note: a sucker here is not a dupe but a machine that sucks, and this is how it clears dust

explanation.definitionFit: Cleaning by suction means drawing dust up with a powered household appliance.

clue.text: Dug up to rid resident of rebellious activity

indicators.note: rebellion turns things upside down, so these letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A protest was organised to drive out a troublesome local.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebellious activity' rearranges RID RESIDENT; 'to' and 'of' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Disinterred means exhumed, taken out of the grave or ground.

clue.text: Clearing off grid chasing

indicators.note: off in the sense of wrong or awry, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Escaping from a pursuit across a city's street grid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clearing off' reads as one phrase meaning leaving, but it splits: 'off' is the anagram signal for the next two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Discharging a debt or duty means settling it, paying it off completely.

clue.text: It's scandalous that god is elegant

parts.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld
graceful means elegant

explanation.surface: Someone is shocked that a deity should be so stylish.
explanation.walkthrough: DIS is Pluto's Roman name; 'It's', 'that' and 'is' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Disgraceful conduct is shameful, the kind of thing that causes outrage.

clue.text: He encourages one to stand and drink

definitions.text: He encourages one to stand and drink

parts.words: He encourages one to stand and drink
parts.note: at a formal dinner this official calls the guests to rise and raise glasses in honour of someone

explanation.definitionFit: At a banquet the master of ceremonies announces the speakers and proposes toasts.

clue.text: Is back in motor club land

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the motoring club letters

parts.note: AA is the Automobile Association, a British motoring organisation

indicators.note: back means the word Is is read in reverse

explanation.surface: A motoring club has returned to its home territory.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' turns 'Is' round and 'in' puts it inside the letters of the Automobile Association, a British breakdown service.
explanation.definitionFit: Asia is the largest continent, a vast landmass.

clue.text: Novice to eat endless dirt

indicators.note: to eat something is to take it inside, so the first piece swallows the second
without ends, so the first and last letters of the word are dropped

explanation.surface: A beginner is told to eat a mouthful of muck as an initiation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips D and T from 'dirt' to leave IR, which TO is made to 'eat'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiro, also spelt tyro, is a beginner or learner in some field.

clue.text: Release putting clans up in chaos

indicators.note: letters in chaos are thrown into disorder and rearranged

explanation.surface: Freeing the clans stirs them up into anarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in chaos' rearranges CLANS UP; 'putting' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To unclasp is to unfasten a clasp, letting go or freeing what it held.

clue.text: Good fate of trial scheme

parts.note: pi is short for pious, so good
one's lot is one's fate or destiny

explanation.surface: Whether a test run turns out well is a matter of fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: PI (pious) is a crossword staple for good; 'of' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A pilot is a small-scale experimental run tried before a full launch.

clue.text: Development of ontogenesis loses nine minions

indicators.note: the development of something reshapes it, so the letters are reworked

explanation.surface: Biological growth from embryo is said to shed nine underlings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loses' tells you to remove the letters of NINE from ONTOGENESIS; 'Development of' rearranges the OTOGESS left.
explanation.definitionFit: Stooges are subordinates who do others' bidding, flunkeys or lackeys.

clue.text: Hard to find suitcase on railway terminus

parts.note: the case of the word suit, its first and last letters

indicators.note: a terminus is the end of the line, so the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A traveller struggles to locate luggage at the end of a train line.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'suitcase' as 'suit case', the outer letters of SUIT: ST. 'terminus' takes Y from 'railway'; 'to find' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stony means as hard as stone, rocky and unyielding.

clue.text: High stake brings first to last in the lists?

indicators.note: the opening letter is shifted round to the end of the word

parts.note: a stilt is a tall post or pole raising something high

explanation.surface: A tall wager moves a leader to the bottom of the rankings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brings first to last' moves the S of STILT to the end. The lists were the fenced arena for jousting; 'in' is a link and 'lists' is not a set of rankings.
explanation.definitionFit: A tilt is a joust, and the tilts were the jousting ground, an old name for the tiltyard.

clue.text: Insane about the last drink

indicators.note: the first piece goes about, or around, the second

parts.note: mad means insane

indicators.note: the last letter of the word just before it

explanation.surface: A crazed drinker orders one final round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last' takes E from 'the'; MAD goes 'about' it.
explanation.definitionFit: Mead is an ancient alcoholic beverage brewed from fermented honey.

clue.text: Perfect tree to offload on to someone?

annotationWithheld.why: Clue as held: 'Perfect tree to offload on to someone? (4)'. 'tree' and 'offload on to someone' (palm off) define PALM, but 'Perfect' has no job and no source confirms the wording.
annotationWithheld.clue: Perfect tree to offload on to someone?

clue.text: Establish kitty had nothing

indicators.note: the kitty had, or held, the other piece inside it

parts.note: a kitty is a pooled fund of money
O is the round figure zero, nothing

explanation.surface: Someone opening an account finds the shared money pot is empty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'had' puts O (nothing) inside FUND; 'kitty' is not a cat.
explanation.definitionFit: To found an institution is to set it up or create it.

clue.text: Charity events with pleasure ladders

parts.note: fun means pleasure or enjoyment
ladders in tights are runs

explanation.surface: Fundraisers entertain with gleeful climbing ladders.
explanation.walkthrough: A ladder is the British word for a run in stockings or tights; 'with' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: These are sponsored jogs held to raise money for good causes.

clue.text: The most stupid bit covering pies

indicators.note: the first piece covers the second, wrapping around it

parts.note: a dot is a tiny bit

explanation.surface: A small speck of pastry crust tops some pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'covering' tells you the small mark goes around the pies, one letter either side.
explanation.definitionFit: Dopey means dim-witted, so the dopiest person is the slowest-witted of all.

clue.text: Lout has cut dog's head off exiting computer

indicators.note: the second piece cuts into the first, splitting it open
the head of a word is its first letter, which is taken away

parts.note: dog's read as dogs

explanation.surface: A thug has docked a dog's tail end, or rather its head.
explanation.walkthrough: 'head off' removes the first letter of the dogs, and 'cut' puts what is left inside the lout after its first letter; 'has' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Logging out ends a user's session on a system, so one who logs out is leaving it.

clue.text: War of roses city ruler's deliveries

parts.note: York gave its name to one house in the Wars of the Roses
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the monarch, with the possessive S

explanation.surface: A medieval civil war leaves a city's king handing over parcels.
explanation.walkthrough: The Wars of the Roses were fought between the houses of York and Lancaster. A yorker is a cricket ball pitched right at the batter's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a bowler's deliveries include balls of this kind, aimed to land at the base of the bat.

clue.text: Relatively speaking she is a gold nut case

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

indicators.note: the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

explanation.surface: A woman is described as a golden eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nut case' looks like 'crazy person'; read it as the case of NUT, its first and last letters. 'is a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a female relative, the sister of a parent.

clue.text: Bush say can go into Oxford to keep order

definitions.text: can go into Oxford to keep order

explanation.surface: A shrub, or a city's way of keeping discipline.
explanation.walkthrough: An Oxford here is a laced shoe, not the university city, and a shoe tree keeps it in shape.
explanation.definitionFit: A bush is a woody plant like a small tree; a shoe tree is a shaped insert put in a shoe so it keeps its form.

clue.text: Little Edward's party served starchy food

parts.note: Ed is a short form of Edward
a do is a party

explanation.surface: A young boy's celebration served up some carbohydrates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Eddo is another name for taro, a tropical tuber eaten as a staple.

clue.text: Ponder on issue of goddess of memory

explanation.surface: Someone thinks about a matter connected with the deity of remembering.
explanation.walkthrough: In Greek myth the nine Muses were the daughters, or issue, of Mnemosyne, goddess of memory; 'on' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To muse is to think deeply or reflect; each of the Muses was a child of Mnemosyne.

clue.text: Old Israeli statesman out of the mire

indicators.note: out in the sense of disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A veteran politician from Israel is pulled out of the swamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' rearranges MIRE; 'of the' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Golda Meir was Israel's prime minister from 1969 to 1974.

clue.text: First floor track status

parts.note: ground in the sense of a course or tract of land covered
level means standing or rank

explanation.surface: A report on the state of the running track on the bottom storey.
explanation.walkthrough: In American usage the first floor is the one at street height, which British speakers call the ground floor.
explanation.definitionFit: The storey at street height sits at the same height as the surrounding earth.

clue.text: Air-force weapons that send pulses flying

definitions.text: Air-force weapons that send pulses flying

parts.words: Air-force weapons that send pulses flying
parts.note: not military aircraft guns but toy tubes powered by a puff of breath that fire dried legumes

explanation.definitionFit: These are children's toy blowpipes that fire small dried seeds.
